source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20. NOTE: WebFetch/direct-URL fetching was blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED) for every domain in this execution environment (Screener.in, company IR sites, BSE/NSE archives, news sites) — all data below was reconstructed from WebSearch result snippets and third-party summaries rather than direct AR PDF reads, so confidence is uniformly Low.

rural.evidence: Company cites PMAY-Gramin (2 crore additional rural houses targeted through FY29) and the Jal Jeevan Mission (rural overhead water tanks built with structural tubes) as demand drivers; third-party estimates put ~64% of revenue linked to the housing/residential segment, but no precise rural-revenue % found in primary disclosures reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: Analyst commentary links growth to government infrastructure capex (FY26-27 Union Budget capex ~Rs1,22,000 crore; National Infrastructure Pipeline) for bridges, metro, airports and PMAY housing, but no company-disclosed % of revenue from government projects found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company uses short-term commercial paper (e.g. Rs100 crore at 6.15% for 64 days) for working capital; no floating-rate liability % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Business is overwhelmingly domestic (exports to ~30 countries but no export % disclosed), implying limited FX exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Industry commentary describes structural steel tubes/profiles broadly as a PLI (specialty steel) beneficiary category, but no company-specific confirmation found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Historically uses foreign exchange forward contracts, including cash-flow hedges, to manage USD/GBP/EUR exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix: Americas 53.9%, EMEA 34.7%, India ~10% (revenue grew 33.7% YoY to Rs12,051 crore), implying ~90% foreign-currency-denominated revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits NFIL's export-led business"; global pharma and agro companies reportedly awarding 20-30% of annual orders to Indian manufacturers to reduce China concentration; CDMO segment expected to cross $100mn revenue by FY27.

inr_exposure.evidence: 77% of revenue from exports in Q4FY25 (23% domestic) implies majority foreign-currency (largely USD/EUR) denominated revenue; specific hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company has qualified for aspects of bulk-drug/API-linked PLI sub-schemes but these have not directly benefited most specialty chemical names like Navin Fluorine; capacity expansion (Dahej, Dewas) attributed more to the China+1 shift than direct PLI incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Divi's continues to attract partnerships with multinational pharmaceutical companies looking to diversify their supply chains and reduce dependency on China"; custom-synthesis (CRAMS) mix has risen toward ~56-60% of product mix, partly attributed to global innovators' China-diversification strategies, though not framed with explicit quantified attribution.

crude_exposure.evidence: Solvent costs (petroleum-derived, largely imported from the Middle East, e.g. methanol) have doubled/tripled in price due to Middle East geopolitical situations, pressuring raw material costs; company has passed on higher solvent costs via generic API price increases. No exact raw-material % tied to crude found.

inr_exposure.evidence: 88% of FY25 revenue from exports, with Europe (52.3%) and North America (17.1%) the largest markets, implying substantial EUR/USD revenue exposure; specific hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation disclosed; Divi's is an established generic-API/CRAMS exporter rather than a new-molecule domestic manufacturer typically targeted by India's Bulk Drug PLI incentive structure.

rural.evidence: Expansion into tier-2 catchments (Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi/Indore) targets underpenetrated central/northern India markets; Cluster 2 (Lucknow, Patna, Noida) grew revenue 28% and EBITDA 40% (ex-Noida) vs Cluster 1's 10%/13%, with Patna carrying a higher share of government-scheme patients via a PPP model.

govt_capex.evidence: Medanta Lucknow is empanelled under Ayushman Bharat and the Deen Dayal Health Scheme; the network secured CGHS empanelment in October 2024. Patna's PPP-model hospital has a notably higher government-scheme patient share. No consolidated % of revenue from government schemes found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Debt-to-equity reportedly fell from 46.6% to 15.8% over five years, with debt well covered by operating cash flow (~113%); floating- vs fixed-rate borrowing split not found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/medical-value-travel patient revenue reportedly grew ~20% YoY in a recent quarter, but no disclosed % of total revenue from international patients found.

govt_capex.evidence: "Higher capex in infrastructure, railways, renewables, power distribution, water, energy, commercial buildings, and metals are likely to provide necessary opportunities for growth... government's continued focus on low carbon technology and energy transition across infrastructure, localization and transportation augur well for the company's divisions." Data centers and railways cited as key CY2024 order-growth drivers; order backlog Rs9,380cr (+12% YoY) at Dec 2024.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India Limited reported no borrowings in 2023, 2022, 2021 and 2020 (net-cash company).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Hedges material currency exposures via forward foreign exchange contracts with third-party financial institutions.
inr_exposure.evidence: Parent-level ABB also uses cross-currency interest rate swaps to manage FX/interest-rate risk; India-specific hedge ratios not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence of ABB India participating in any PLI scheme; core electrification/automation product categories are not primary PLI-covered sectors.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Exports at 14,054 MINR constitute ~8.3% of total sales in 2024-25... close to 69% of the total products exported to Robert Bosch, Germany." Company aims to lift export contribution from 8% to 8.5% via favorable product mix — export scaling is intra-group/Europe-oriented rather than an explicit China+1 diversification narrative; commentary also notes Bosch India faces China competition from excess Chinese manufacturing capacity as a headwind.

rural.evidence: "8% expansion in the two-wheeler market driven by festive demand and improving rural cash flows"; Mobility sector product sales +7.0% YoY in FY24-25 aided by tractor-segment growth.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cost of materials consumed was 63.4% of revenue from operations in FY24-25 (down from 64.8% in FY23-24); key raw materials cited are steel and aluminum rather than direct crude-oil-linked inputs.

inr_exposure.evidence: Majority of ~8.3% export revenue is intra-Bosch-group (69% to Robert Bosch, Germany), suggesting EUR-denominated exposure rather than pure USD; explicit hedging policy text not located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch Limited is an approved beneficiary under the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components (Champion OEM/Component Champion Incentive Scheme, approved 15 March 2022) for Advanced Automotive Technology products; revenue benefit not separately quantified.

china_plus_one.evidence: Narrative centers on Chinese steel import/dumping risk rather than a China+1 diversification tailwind: management stated it does not see a surge in import bookings, expressing confidence authorities would act if a surge occurred; imports moderated Q3 to Q4 FY25. Company's focus is specialised/high-margin steel (automotive, alloys, CRGO, stainless) for the domestic market.

govt_capex.evidence: India's domestic steel demand is strong, driven by increased infrastructure spending — Interim Budget FY2024-25 raised infrastructure spending 11% to Rs11 lakh crore, expected to boost domestic steel demand; FY25 capex of Rs6,584cr largely toward integrated capacity expansion (23.65 to 24.20 MTPA) in Odisha/West Bengal.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company described as almost debt free with total debt ~Rs10.9 billion against a debt-to-equity ratio of ~9.2%; floating-rate share not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs are iron ore and coal (for sponge iron/pellets/billets/TMT/wire rod/ferro-alloys production); specific raw-material cost as % of revenue not found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (proxy for USD-linked revenue) were ~10.63% of turnover in the period reviewed; explicit hedging policy text not located.

pli_scheme.evidence: "Shyam Metalics Flat Products has been selected to invest under the production linked incentive (PLI) scheme for specialty steel" (Rs6,322 crore outlay scheme FY2023-24 to FY2027-28, covering coated/plated steel, high-strength steel, alloy steel, electrical steel); revenue benefit not separately quantified.

inr_exposure.evidence: GSK Pharma derives 98% of revenue from the domestic market vs 2% from international markets — minimal direct USD revenue exposure given overwhelmingly domestic sales mix (vaccines ~20% / general medicines ~80% of FY24 sales).

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence of GSK Pharma India participating in a PLI scheme; company is a domestically-focused formulations/vaccines business rather than a bulk-drug/API manufacturer (the PLI-covered category).

rural.evidence: Company has an extensive pan-India distribution network offering reach across urban and rural markets, adapting distribution strategy to regional dynamics; recent expansion includes doubling retail touchpoints in Uttar Pradesh. Maharashtra and Karnataka together contribute ~40% of total volume. No rural-specific revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Debt-to-equity ratio was ~0.0 in both FY24 and FY23 (near-zero leverage); finance costs fell 26.9% YoY in FY24 and interest coverage improved to 25.4x from 13.3x.

inr_exposure.evidence: Predominantly a domestic Indian spirits business (NSV Rs10,692cr in FY23-24, +10.5% YoY, driven by premiumisation); direct USD revenue exposure appears minimal but not explicitly quantified.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company is building own API manufacturing (Vizag facility, R&D on 90+ APIs) partly to reduce reliance on Chinese API sourcing (currently ~24% of exports sourced from China); framed as backward integration/self-reliance rather than an explicit China+1 revenue-growth narrative.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported as virtually debt-free with large cash/liquid asset balance (~Rs1,471cr cash, Rs2,726cr liquid assets), suggesting minimal rate sensitivity, but no explicit floating-rate liability % found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No formal hedging/forward contracts; relies on natural hedge (China/dollar-linked sourcing) and dynamic product pricing in distributor warehouses to absorb FX moves.
inr_exposure.evidence: Caplin Point does not engage in hedging contracts; relies on a natural hedge with operations in China and other dollar-based markets, adjusting product prices in its warehouses to offset losses.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that Caplin Point itself is a PLI (bulk drug) scheme beneficiary.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Hedges receivables in major currencies, primarily USD and EUR, to mitigate FX fluctuation impact on financials.
inr_exposure.evidence: OFSS manages foreign currency risk by hedging receivables in major currencies (USD and EUR); US contributed ~29% of revenue, Europe 16%, Asia-Pacific 18%.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI schemes in India target manufacturing sectors (electronics, IT hardware, pharma, autos); pure software/IT services like OFSS are not covered by any PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industrial Product Division has concentrated efforts on exports of value-added specialty films; shift from low-margin commodity polyester films to high-margin specialty films (SCF, PPF, shrink films, ~88% of Q1FY25 sales) with export orientation of 77%, competing mainly against foreign (including Chinese) players.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Reported as having zero net debt with ~Rs650 crore cash reserves as of March 2025, implying minimal rate sensitivity, but no floating-rate liability % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Major raw materials like PTA & MEG come from crude oil, whose prices are volatile (company mitigates this with forward contracts & long term agreements); key suppliers are Indian refiners like Reliance Industries with import-parity pricing arrangements. No explicit raw-material-cost % found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses forward contracts and long-term supply agreements to manage crude-linked raw material cost volatility; no explicit FX-hedging % disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company derives ~77% of revenue from exports, with US, Europe and Middle East cited as its largest markets; maintains US and UK subsidiaries for international distribution.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable found for specialty polyester films manufacturing.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company has long pursued export/overseas expansion (plants in Indonesia since 2005, Vietnam since 2009) with a stated goal of doubling export revenue as a buffer against domestic-only dependence; no explicit China+1 framing or revenue attribution found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~Rs2,537cr, Debt/Equity ~0.37x, net debt ~1.2x EBITDA, EBIT/interest coverage ~8.6x; company has issued fixed-rate bonds (~7.1-7.12% coupon) alongside bank borrowings, but no explicit floating-rate liability % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Auto components use plastics and rubber parts, which are petrochemical/crude-oil-derived inputs exposed to crude price volatility, per general industry context; no company-specific raw-material-cost % found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Cited among auto-component makers expected to receive incentives under the Auto PLI scheme (Zero Emission Vehicle / Advanced Automotive Technology components) starting FY27, positioned as a beneficiary of PLI and rising EV/ADAS/premium-SUV component demand; no revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Engineers India is a Government of India PSU under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (~51.3% promoter/govt holding); portfolio dominated by oil & gas engineering consultancy/EPC, having worked on 20 of 23 operational Indian refineries; order book (~Rs6,500cr consultancy + ~Rs4,659cr turnkey as of Sep 2024) concentrated in PSU oil-major clients — HPCL and associates alone were ~33% of outstanding order book as of Sep 2023; growth explicitly tied to oil & gas segment capex cycles, with diversification underway into LNG, fertilizers, renewables, green hydrogen/ammonia.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has no external debt apart from lease liabilities and mobilisation advances (total-outside-liabilities/net-worth ~0.95x as of March 2024), implying very low rate sensitivity, though no floating-rate liability % is disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not a raw-material consumer in the traditional sense (engineering/EPC consultancy); order flow/business volume is indirectly linked to crude oil price cycles via client (PSU oil major) capex decisions — no direct raw-material-cost exposure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme relevant to engineering consultancy/EPC services found.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural revenue % disclosed. Nykaa's B2B Superstore (wholesale) segment now serves ~276k retailers across ~1,100 cities (vs 112k/195k in FY23/FY24), with management citing deeper Tier-2/Tier-3+ penetration as a growth driver for FY25-30 BPC GMV CAGR target of ~25%.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt reported at ~Rs9.9B with finance costs up ~29.5% YoY in FY25; no floating-vs-fixed rate borrowing breakdown found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar operates nine manufacturing facilities across India, USA, Mexico and China, framed around diversifying across products, customers and geographies (incl. 2025 acquisition of Escorts Kubota's railway business). No explicit 'China+1 sourcing' framing found, but export/geographic diversification narrative is present alongside strong EV/BEV export order momentum (BEV revenue +38% YoY in FY25).

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material inputs are steel/forgings for driveline components, not crude oil-linked; no explicit crude-oil raw-material % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Financial statements reference a Cash Flow Hedge Reserve and Foreign Currency Translation Reserve, indicating active FX hedging, but specific policy detail/percentage not extracted.
inr_exposure.evidence: Most recent disclosed geographic split (Q2 FY26 investor presentation, not FY25 AR): India ~41%, North America ~30%, Europe ~24% of revenue. FY2024-25 annual-report-specific geography note could not be confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: First Indian auto-component supplier to receive Auto PLI scheme certification (hub wheel drive motor for e-2-wheelers, Feb 2024); subsequently certified for three additional EV traction motor products in 2025. Revenue contribution/quantum of PLI incentive not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield/Eicher Motors' export narrative centers on new-market entry and premiumization (new CKD plants in Thailand and planned Brazil; #1 in UK, #2 Argentina, #3 Brazil), not on China+1 supply-chain diversification.

rural.evidence: Rural sales account for a third of Royal Enfield's sales and over half of the country's two-wheeler industry; rural demand cited as continuing to outpace urban growth through FY25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher Motors carries minimal/near-nil debt (strong net-cash balance sheet); specific floating-rate liability % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs include steel, aluminum and rubber (tyres) with indirect crude-oil linkage via rubber/polymer costs; no explicit crude-oil-linked raw material % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Consolidated exports (units) up 29.7% YoY to 100,136 units in FY25; international business revenue of ~Rs2,546cr, up 38% YoY, against total FY25 revenue of ~Rs188 billion (~10% share, consistent with the 90% domestic/10% overseas split).

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors is listed as an approved participant under the Champion OEM Incentive component of India's Auto PLI scheme; revenue/incentive quantum specific to Eicher not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company explicitly frames itself around a 'China-plus-one' strategy, sourcing less than 20% of raw material inputs from China (well below peers); CEO quoted: "We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones." Positioned as an alternative for global biotech/pharma majors diversifying supply chains away from China, tied directly to CRDMO order growth and margin resilience.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed 85% of revenue from operations for the most recent reported fiscal year, serving customers across 50 countries; CRDMO segment (~83% of revenue) caters primarily to regulated markets (US, Europe), while the smaller Specialty Ingredients segment also serves semi-regulated markets. Specific hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No direct disclosure found confirming Anthem Biosciences as a certified beneficiary of the government's PLI Bulk Drugs/API scheme; Anthem operates as a CRDMO/CRAMS business model, distinct from that scheme's typical beneficiary profile.

rural.evidence: The four-year CAGR of Tier-III and beyond cities was 17%, compared to the 14% overall revenue CAGR, with these smaller/rural markets now contributing 3% of Dr Lal's revenues; FY25 growth also cited as volume-led with organic expansion into Tier-III/Tier-IV towns and newer West/South regions (national footprint ~280 labs, ~5,700 collection centres).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company described as almost debt free with a net cash position; negligible floating-rate liability exposure implied, though no specific % disclosed.
